title: Proof & 50M-Line Lean 4 Formalization of the Courtade–Kumar Conjecture
whyItMatters: Resolved information theory’s flagship 2013 Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture in full generality—confirming dictator functions maximize mutual information over noisy channels—with a 50-million-line Lean 4 proof.
summary: Announced in September 2026 (arXiv:2609.24184) and detailed in Google Research’s November 13, 2026 Antigravity /teamwork report, researchers from Google Research, CUHK, USC, and CMU resolved Thomas Courtade and Gowtham Kumar’s 2013 Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture in full generality—proving that when a uniformly random bit string passes through a binary symmetric noisy channel, no 1-bit Boolean function preserves more mutual information than a dictator function copying a single coordinate. After Gemini first found counterexamples to an earlier generalized candidate from CUHK, human theorists reduced the problem to a 14-variable optimization and analytical lower bound; Gemini 4 Argon and /teamwork’s Long Proof (Stellar Colosseum) harness then partitioned the parameter space, derived most new analytical bounds and interval-arithmetic certificates, autonomously extended the proof from balanced to unbalanced Boolean functions, and formalized the complete proof in ~50 million lines of Lean 4.
technicalHighlights: Settled information theory’s 2013 Courtade–Kumar Conjecture across all noise levels and both balanced and unbalanced Boolean functions.

Gemini first falsified an earlier generalized conjecture, then Gemini 4 Argon + /teamwork derived analytical bounds, interval-arithmetic certificates, and the autonomous extension to unbalanced functions.
Published both the arXiv manuscript (arXiv:2609.24184) and a public Lean 4 formalization repository (dpwoodru/general-courtade-kumar-lean) spanning ~50 million lines of machine-checked code.
caveats: Because the machine-checked formalization relies on extensive interval-arithmetic case partitions totaling ~50 million lines of Lean 4, independent mathematicians are working on extracting shorter, fully human-readable analytical simplifications.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves one of the best-known open conjectures in modern information theory and Boolean Fourier analysis since 2013.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates scalable human–multi-agent mathematical collaboration (Antigravity /teamwork + Lean 4) handling high-dimensional analytical optimization proofs.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked in Lean 4 with public GitHub repository, arXiv manuscript, and active academic review alongside concurrent independent human work.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed a 14-variable analytical partition and unbalanced-function extension that had resisted a decade of manual attacks.
